review: 1:1 לִבְנֵי אָדָם דּוֹד אֶחָד — the Arabic is 'لِلْوَرَى خِلٌّ وَحِيد' (to mankind, one friend); the fronted dative is deliberate for the 8-syllable line.
2:4 בְּעוֹד הָיִינוּ צָרָיו — 'while we were still His enemies', echoing Rom 5:10 (בְּעוֹדֵנוּ אֹיְבִים).
3:2 פּוֹדֵה חַטָּאִים הוּא — construct participle, 'He is the Ransomer of sinners'; the Arabic also has 'رَبُّنَا' (our Lord), dropped to keep the line at 6.
4:1 עוֹד מְעַט מִזְעָר — Isaiah 26:20 idiom for 'soon'; the fuller form is used so the line does not fall short of the tune.

4:4 כִּי אַהֲבָתוֹ רָבָה מִכָּל־תְּאוּרָה — 'for His love is greater than all telling', the user's own replacement for the earlier מִכָּל־סִפּוּר; it is longer than the tune's other 4:4 lines, so it will read as a deliberate broadening at the close.
